title: Where acquisitions sits in the deal
alt: The deal pipeline in seven steps: marketing, cold caller, lead manager, acquisitions (highlighted), transaction coordinator and title, dispositions, closing.

title: The follow-up ladder
alt: Follow-up ladder: hot within 24 hours then every 2 to 3 days; warm in 1 week then every 2 weeks; nurture in 30 days then monthly; cold in 90 days then every 3 to 6 months; do-not-call never.

title: Scoring a lead on the four pillars
alt: Four pillars scorecard: motivation, timeline, condition and price each scored 1 to 3; totals of 10 to 12 hot, 7 to 9 warm, 5 to 6 nurture, 4 dead for now.

title: How a lead moves through the CRM
alt: Lead status flow: new, attempting, contacted, qualified, appointment set, offer made, under contract; from any step a lead can move to nurture, dead or do-not-call.

title: The order you work the queue
alt: Queue order: 1 brand-new inbound leads, 2 scheduled callbacks, 3 hot leads waiting on a next step, 4 today's follow-ups, 5 attempting leads, 6 cold lists in power-hour blocks.

title: The 10 stages of the acquisition call
alt: The ten stages of the call: intro and permission, upfront agreement, rapport, property walkthrough, motivation and pain, timeline, money and decision makers, price, offer and negotiation, close and next steps.

title: Where the time goes on a 30-minute call
alt: Time on a 30-minute call: open and rapport 10%, discovery and qualifying 45%, gap summary 5%, presenting the offer 20%, price, objections and close 20%.

title: A house in four layers
alt: A house in four layers: interior (cosmetic), systems, envelope (roof most common big repair) and structure (most expensive, can kill a deal), with cost rising toward structure.

title: Linda's MAO, step by step
alt: MAO waterfall for Linda's house: ARV $215,000, times 70% is $150,500, minus $59,000 repairs gives $91,500 end buyer price, minus $15,000 fee gives $76,500 MAO; opening offer $65,000 to $68,000.

title: What a flipper can pay for Linda's house
alt: Flipper's maximum: of a $215,000 ARV, rehab $59,000, profit target $32,250, selling costs $17,200, holding $9,000, buying costs $1,913, leaving about $95,600; with a $74,000 contract the fee room is about $17,500 to $21,000.

title: One objection system, three lengths
alt: Objection system in three lengths: full six steps pause, acknowledge, clarify, isolate, respond, re-close; short four steps acknowledge, clarify, respond, advance; quick three steps acknowledge, ask, answer then check in.

title: The four numbers in every negotiation
alt: Four numbers on Linda's deal: opening offer $68,000, signed $74,000, walk-away MAO $76,500, asking price $180,000; if her real minimum is below the MAO there is a deal, above it cash will not work.

title: Choosing the deal structure
alt: Exit decision tree: cash if there is equity at or under MAO; otherwise novation, subject-to, seller finance, or short sale, and if none fit, a scheduled follow-up or referral.

title: The timeline of a typical cash deal
alt: Cash deal timeline: day 0 contract signed, days 1 to 3 earnest money, days 3 to 10 title search, title commitment, curative work, dispo assigns or double closes, settlement statement approved, then signing, funding and recording.

title: Who is at the closing table
alt: Closing players: the title company or escrow in the center, surrounded by the transaction coordinator, closing attorney, underwriter, notary or mobile signer, and county recorder.

title: The general path to foreclosure
alt: Foreclosure path: missed payments, the 120-day line, first filing, sale date set, auction, after the sale; judicial foreclosure is slower and goes through court, non-judicial is faster under a power of sale.

title: Land access, best to worst
alt: Land access ladder: public road frontage is best, then private road with a recorded agreement, recorded easement, physical path only (risky), and landlocked (big discount).

title: The dispo clock
alt: Dispo clock: hand-off and underwriting on day 0 to 1, package by day 2, hot list then full blast days 2 to 3, showings days 3 to 6, offers days 5 to 7, assignment signed days 7 to 9, close day 10 to 30; inspection period often 7 to 14 days.

title: From marketing dollars to closed deals
alt: Marketing funnel: 120 leads become 4 contracts (3.3%) and 3 closed deals (75%); spend $6,000, cost per lead $50, cost per contract $1,500, cost per deal $2,000, average fee $11,000, marketing return 450%.

title: How certification works
alt: Certification path: pass modules 1 to 19 at 85%, the final exam at 85%, three role-plays (40+ each, one 45+), the compliance quiz at 90% and the capstone deal file; then certified for one year and renewed yearly.
